questions.question: A number line is drawn with every whole number from −8 to 8 marked, and all the spaces between marks are equal. Point A sits 3 spaces to the left of 0, and point B sits 6 spaces to the left of 0. Which statement about A and B is true?
options: B is less than A, because B is farther to the left of 0.
A is less than B, because A is closer to 0.
Neither one is greater, because both points are negative.
B is greater than A, because 6 is greater than 3.
questions.explain: On a number line, whatever sits farther left is the smaller number, so −6 (point B) is less than −3 (point A). The usual trap is comparing only the digits 6 and 3 and forgetting that the minus sign flips which side of 0 you are on.

questions.question: A number line has every whole number from −10 to 10 marked with equal spaces. Point R is 7 spaces to the left of 0, point S is 2 spaces to the left of 0, and point T is 1 space to the right of 0. Which list shows R, S and T in order from least to greatest?
questions.explain: Reading a number line from left to right always gives least to greatest, so the order is −7, then −2, then 1. A common trap is sorting the negatives by their digits and writing −2 before −7, but −7 is farther left, so it is the smaller number.

questions.question: A number line shows every whole number from −10 to 10 with equal spaces. Both −9 and −4 are marked on it. Which statement is true?
options: −4 is closer to 0, but −9 is the greater number.
−9 is closer to 0, and −9 is the greater number.
−4 is closer to 0, and −4 is the greater number.
−9 is closer to 0, but −4 is the greater number.
questions.explain: −4 is only 4 spaces from 0 while −9 is 9 spaces away, so −4 is both closer to 0 and farther right, which makes it greater. The trap is thinking a bigger digit means a bigger number: for negatives, the farther you go from 0, the smaller the number gets.

questions.question: A number line has 0 in the middle, with every whole number from −6 to 6 marked at equal spaces. Where do all the negative numbers sit, and what happens to their value as you keep moving that way?
options: They sit to the left of 0, and the numbers keep the same value, since only the sign changes.
They sit to the left of 0, and the numbers get larger as you move farther left.
They sit to the right of 0, and the numbers get smaller as you move farther right.
They sit to the left of 0, and the numbers get smaller as you move farther left.
questions.explain: Negative numbers live to the left of 0, and every step left makes the number smaller: −1, −2, −3 and so on go down in value. The trap is reading −6 as 'six of something' and thinking it grows as you move left, when it is really dropping below 0.

questions.question: Which one of these comparisons is true?
questions.explain: Picture each pair on a number line: −6 sits farther left than −1, so −6 < −1 is the true one. The trap is judging by the digits, which makes people write things like −9 > −3, but −9 is farther from 0 on the negative side, so it is smaller.

questions.question: Which list shows the integers −7, 2, −13 and 0 in order from GREATEST to LEAST?
questions.explain: Greatest to least means reading the number line from right to left: 2, then 0, then −7, then −13. The trap is putting −13 ahead of −7 because 13 looks bigger; on the number line −13 is farther left, so it is the smallest of the four.

questions.question: Which symbol makes this statement true?   −14 ___ −41
options: No symbol works, because you cannot compare two negative numbers.
questions.explain: −14 is only 14 units left of 0 while −41 is 41 units left, so −14 sits to the right and is the greater number: −14 > −41. The trap is comparing 14 with 41 as if the minus signs were not there.

questions.question: Which integer is greater than −6 and also less than −2?
questions.explain: On the number line, the integers strictly between −6 and −2 are −5, −4 and −3, so −4 works. The trap is choosing −7 or −8 because 7 and 8 sit between nothing useful; those numbers are actually farther left than −6, which makes them smaller, not in between.

questions.question: One January morning the temperature was −11 °C in Prince George, −4 °C in Kamloops and −19 °C in Fort Nelson. Which town was the WARMEST that morning, and why?
options: Kamloops, because −4 is the closest to 0 on the number line, so it is the greatest temperature.
Fort Nelson, because −19 is the biggest number of the three.
Prince George, because −11 is the middle value of the three.
Fort Nelson, because it is the farthest away from 0.
questions.explain: Warmest means greatest, which is the temperature farthest to the RIGHT on the number line, and −4 °C is the closest to 0, so Kamloops was warmest. The trap is picking −19 because 19 is the largest digit string, but a temperature farther from 0 on the negative side is colder, not warmer.

questions.question: Off the coast near Tofino, a scuba diver is at an elevation of −18 m and a crab is resting on the sea floor at −25 m. Sea level is 0 m. Which one is closer to sea level, and by how much?
options: The crab, because −25 is greater than −18, and it is 7 m closer.
The diver, because −18 is closer to 0 than −25, and the diver is 7 m closer.
The diver, but only by 43 m.
The crab, because it is farther from 0, and it is 43 m closer.
questions.explain: First compare positions: −18 sits to the right of −25 on the number line, so the diver is nearer sea level; then find the gap, 25 − 18 = 7 m. Two traps here are thinking −25 is the greater elevation because 25 is a bigger digit, and adding 18 + 25 instead of subtracting to find the distance between them.

questions.question: Four students check their school lunch-card balances: Maya −$8, Owen −$3, Sam −$12, and Priya $0. Who owes the most money, and who has the greatest balance?
options: Owen owes the most, and Sam has the greatest balance.
Sam owes the most, and Owen has the greatest balance.
Sam owes the most, and Priya has the greatest balance.
Owen owes the most, and Priya has the greatest balance.
questions.explain: Owing the most means the balance farthest LEFT of 0, which is −$12 (Sam), and the greatest balance is the one farthest right, which is $0 (Priya). The trap is treating −$3 as the biggest debt or forgetting that $0, while not much, is still greater than every negative balance.

questions.question: Nina says: 'On my report, −20 must be greater than −5, because 20 is greater than 5.' Which explanation correctly settles this?
options: Nina is wrong, because once you drop the minus signs the two numbers are really the same size.
Nina is right: −20 is 20 units from 0 while −5 is only 5 units from 0, so −20 is the larger number.
Nina is right, because a larger amount owed always means a larger number.
Nina is wrong: on a number line −20 sits farther left than −5, and numbers get smaller as you move left, so −20 < −5.
questions.explain: For negative numbers, being farther from 0 means being farther LEFT, which makes the number smaller, so −20 < −5. The trap is Nina's own reasoning: distance from 0 tells you how big the amount is, but position on the number line tells you which number is greater.
